mechanism: the level-1 cost of the quantiser REPELS the community: the contract's distance between the item's community point and the code's community profile is ADDED to the cost, so the items of one behaviour community are pushed onto different level-1 codes

calls.name: the community term's curved distance
calls.note: The distance between the item's point in the community model's Poincare ball and the code's community profile, in the contract's convention. The profile is the mean of the tangent vectors of the items the code received, mapped back into the ball with the origin exponential; the free branch contributes the Euclidean distance in the same way, and the two are standardised per item and averaged.

coupling.note: The behaviour signal is the community representation; the curve is the contract's Poincare distance between the item's community point and the code's profile. Both enter the level-1 cost matrix that the baseline's assignment rule consumes, and the rule itself is untouched. The term is detached, so it moves the assignment and not the losses. The direction is a repulsion in this arm: a code whose profile is close to the item's community becomes more expensive for that item, which raises the level-1 hard error rate. The campaign's measurement that the recall is ordered backwards by that error rate is the prediction this arm tests.

excluded.surface: the per-item standardisation of the term
excluded.reason: a per-row affine transform of the term's matrix; it is the scale that makes the two terms comparable and it is applied after the distance
a detached statistic of past assignments (a mean of tangent vectors), not a differentiable function of the parameters

excluded.surface: the calibration of the term's weight
excluded.reason: a measured scalar read once from the baseline cost's own spread; it carries no gradient
the baseline's rule is unchanged; the mechanism only changes the cost it consumes
